newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH LEAGUE AND CUP MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH LEAGUE AND CUP MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league and Football Association (F.A.) Cup (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses:
Premier league
Derby County (16) v West Ham (18)

Struggling Derby, without a league since November, welcome back their captain, Croatian international defender Igor Stimac after a hernia operation. Ron Willems, Jacob Laursen are also injured and Ashley Ward is doubtful while Darryl Powell is suspended.

West Ham will give a debut to their new 5.0 million pounds ($8.1 million) club record signing John Hartson, who joined them from Arsenal on Friday. He is expected to form a new spearhead with former Newcastle striker Paul Kitson, who joined the Hammers last week.
Tottenham (10) v Arsenal (3)

England goalkeeper Ian Walker, who was on the losing side against Italy at Wembley on Wednesday, may be out with a shoulder injury for this keenly-anticipated north London derby clash. In defence, Scottish international Colin Calderwood returns after suspension while England internationals Teddy Sheringham and John Scales remain absent, despite returning to training.
Arsenal will be without David Seaman (knee), the No.1 England keeper. He is likely to be replaced by John Lukic while Espen Baardsen of Norway could play for Spurs in goal.
FA Cup fourth round
Blackburn v Coventry

Blackburn, who have not won the F.A. Cup since 1928, hope to take advantage of the early elimination of the four top premier league clubs. Caretaker-coach Tony Parkes hopes to select from a full-strength squad. Striker Chris Sutton is his only doubt as he shrugs off a flu bug.
Coventry, the 1987 winners, will be unchanged from the side which overcame minor league team Woking in the previous round.
Fifth round
Birmingham v Wrexham

This is a first division v second division clash, but with cup-fighters Wrexham hunting their first quarter-final appearance since 1978. Birmingham could be without nine injured players and coach Trevor Francis will notably miss Steve Bruce (hamstring), Swedish winger Anders Limpar (knee), goalscorer Paul Devlin (back) and centre-back Gary Ablett (hamstring).
Wrexham, who knocked out premier club West Ham to progress in the third round, have only one injury doubt -- Phil Hardy with a knee ligament strain.
Chesterfield v Nottingham Forest

Second division Chesterfield, in the fifth round for the first time since 1950, seek a place in the quarter-finals for the first time against Midlands rivalsForest. Chesterfield give a late fitness test to captain Sean Dyche, a former Forest player.

Forest, whose second and last win was in 1959, will be without player-coach Stuart Pearce through suspension. On-loan midfielder Nigel Clough is ineligible and Welsh international striker Dean Saunders returns after missing three games with a hamstring injury.
Leeds v Portsmouth
Leeds, winners of the trophy in 1972, will be without midfielder Lee Bowyer who aggravated an ankle injury during the England under-21's midweek win over Italy.
Portsmouth seek their sixth successive win. They have no fitness worries but star striker Matthias Svensson of Sweden has a slight neck injury.
Manchester City v Middlesbrough

Four-times winners City have enjoyed improved league form under new coach Frank Clark. They recall Middlesbrough-born winger Peter Beagrie and Ian Brightwell and Eddie McGoldrick are back after injury.
Middlesbrough, facing a tricky visit to the first division club in a busy cup week, have goalkeeper Gary Walsh out injured. He will be replaced by Ben Roberts. Brazilian midfielder Emerson is banned.
Wimbledon v QPR

This season's most improved premier team, Wimbledon, won the cup in 1988 and after knocking out holders Manchester United in the fourth round are strongly-fancied to reach the final again. They are also in the English League Cup semifinals.
Wimbledon will be unchanged, but long-term injured Ben Thatcher and Paul Heald remain absent.
Bradford City v Sheffield Wednesday (Sunday 1330)

First division Bradford have not won the Cup since 1911 and are 80-1 outsiders to do so again. Coach Chris Kamara picks from an unchanged squad, including former Wednesday and England winger Chris Waddle, but misses long-term injury victims defender Eddie Youds and striker Gordon Watson, who is likely to take legal action after suffering a broken leg in a recent league fixture.

For three-times winners Wednesday, this will be a difficult Yorkshire derby despite their consistent form in the premier league. Italian forward Benito Carbone is fit again after a two-months absence and Dutch winger Regi Blinker is in contention, but coach David Pleat has doubts over defender Ian Nolan, Welsh midfielder Mark Pembridge and forward Graham Hyde.
Leicester v Chelsea (Sunday 1610)

League cup semifinalists Leicester are enjoying good current form under coach Martin O'Neill, but face a tough test against favourites and Italy-inspired Chelsea. Midfielder Muzzy Izzet will hope to enjoy success against his former club.

Chelsea, with Wembley goalscorer Gianfranco Zola and his Italian team-mate Roberto di Matteo returning to club action, will hope to justify their tag as cup favourites. Coach Ruud Gullit may be without Scottish defender Craig Burley due to a shin injury as he attempts to land Chelsea's first cup success since 1970.
